text:
Ravi: quick heads up - new nightingale-q4 int4 canary showing an odd class of funcall parse failures. seems different from usual EOFs.
Jo: short summary?
Ravi: samples show the model returning an array of results in NDJSON-style streaming, but the batch-slice boundary sometimes splits between objects and the next slice emits a leading `]` or an extra `{` causing parse to fail as "unexpected token" instead of EOF. happens at ~1.9k token requests.
Marina: hmm. int4 quant nudging tokenization again?
Ravi: likely. repro log snippet: 
```
INVOKE id=mx77 model=nightingale-q4 slice=12/48
OUT >> {"tool":"multi_search","items":[{"id":1,"score":0.92},
...<slice ends without closing >...
---next slice---
INVOKE continue id=mx77 slice=13/48
OUT >> {"id":2,"score":0.88}]}
parser: JSONError: unexpected token '{' at position 1
```
Jo: so the intended stream was a single object with items array. boundary produced two top-level `{` objects that the parser treats as separate.
Marina: two new angles to consider: (1) the batch-slice cutter is token-index based; tokenization shift => split inside the array delimiter, (2) NDJSON-like streams are brittle if we expect a single JSON payload.
diag-bot: canary summary: baseline parse failures 0.6% -> canary 3.1% (n=2200). error split: 42% unexpected EOF, 38% unexpected token at slice boundary, 20% other.
Ravi: proposed quick experiments: 
- overlap-replay: have next slice prepend last N tokens (e.g., 16 tokens) of previous slice so if cut was inside an object we still get intact token sequence to reassemble. perf cost small but should reduce boundary errors.
- atomicize-toolcalls: runtime marks toolcall regions and avoid cutting inside top-level arrays/objects where possible (but needs tokenizer-aware cut points).
- sidecar-serialize: instead of raw JSON, serialize tool args as base64 blob inside the stream, decode server-side (heavy but foolproof).
Jo: overlap-replay sounds low-friction. is there a risk of duplicate data causing double-apply? we only replay for streaming reconstruction, not re-invoke downstream tools.
Ravi: yes, replay is purely on the server-side assembler: we merge overlapping tokens and dedupe by token offset. cheap to implement as a flag.
Marina: can we prototype overlap=16 tokens and run micro-canary for 30m with same traffic and reduced slice size (48->32) to isolate perf effect?
ops-bot: created ticket RF-9123 and started a collector to harvest 200 boundary-failure payloads -> /var/tmp/nq4-boundary-samples.tar.gz
Jo: also add telemetry tag: `boundary:overlap_replay_attempted` and `boundary:atomicized` so we can compare.
Ravi: good. fallback plan: if overlap reduces token-boundary errors <60% then try sidecar-serialize for a small percent of traffic (1%) and evaluate.
Marina: timeline?
Ravi: I'll push a toggle to runtime today (off by default). Marina can enable for the canary tomorrow AM and we run 30m micro-canary. I'll post results here.
Jo: one more test: run tokenizer diff between fp16 and int4 on a set of 5k prompt samples to see distribution of token-shift positions, should help tune overlap size.
Ravi: adding that to the ticket. will paste a couple raw failed payloads here as we collect them.
Marina: thanks, keeping thread pinned for updates. :thumbsup:
